description: Self-written report about curl's CMake defaults: one wrong default, one right one, one stated in the negative, and a line in a header that only exists after a build. Covers build flag CONFIRMED + CONTRADICTED (incl. a negated claim) and a precise file/line claim that is CANT_CHECK.

report.title: Default CMake build of curl 8.23.0 enables c-ares
report.body:
With a plain CMake build of curl 8.23.0, c-ares is on by default: ENABLE_ARES defaults to ON. The default build also builds the curl tool (BUILD_CURL_EXE is ON), and cookies stay supported because CURL_DISABLE_COOKIES is not enabled by default.

You can see c-ares is compiled in: line 40 of lib/curl_config.h is `#define USE_ARES 1`.

claim.statement: ENABLE_ARES is ON by default in the CMake build

evidence.note: The only option() or set() for ENABLE_ARES in the CMake files.

claim.statement: BUILD_CURL_EXE is ON by default in the CMake build

evidence.note: The only option() or set() for BUILD_CURL_EXE in the CMake files.

claim.statement: CURL_DISABLE_COOKIES is not enabled by default in the CMake build
claim.source_excerpt: CURL_DISABLE_COOKIES is not enabled by default

evidence.note: Negated claim: expected_enabled is false and the default is OFF. The only option() or set() for it in the CMake files.
lib/curl_config.h is not in git; configure generates it.
CMake generates it too, into the build directory. Its contents depend on the build options, so the source can't settle this claim. Pending the not-found agreement (#10).
